name: Hotel Everest View
summary: Hotel Everest View stands on the Syangboche ridge at about 3,880 m above Namche Bazaar, with rooms and a terrace facing Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam. Opened in 1971, it is the breakfast stop on most Everest helicopter tours and a goal of the Namche rest-day hike.
body: The hotel was built by a Japanese developer, Takashi Miyahara, and opened in 1971 on a ridge chosen for its direct line of sight up the Imja valley to Everest. Low stone buildings blend into the hillside among juniper and dwarf rhododendron, and the dining room and terrace look across the valley to Everest's summit pyramid above the Nuptse–Lhotse ridge, Ama Dablam to the right and Tengboche monastery on its ridge below. Rooms face the same view, so you can watch dawn light on Everest from bed.

Most visitors come for an hour: trekkers walking up from Namche on their acclimatisation day, and helicopter guests who land on the hotel's helipad for breakfast after flying past Kala Patthar. Overnight stays suit travellers who have already spent at least a night or two at Namche or who are on a slow luxury itinerary, because sleeping at 3,880 m soon after arriving from Kathmandu can cause headaches and poor sleep. Food and drink prices reflect the cost of flying supplies in.
why: Rooms and terrace look straight at Everest, Lhotse and Ama Dablam
Helipad on site, used by most Everest heli tours for breakfast
Easy 1.5–2 hour acclimatisation walk from Namche Bazaar

faqs.q: Can I stay overnight at Hotel Everest View?
faqs.a: Yes. The hotel has rooms facing Everest and offers overnight stays. Because it sits at about 3,880 m, we recommend staying only after acclimatising in Namche for a night or two, or on a slow luxury itinerary. Heli guests usually visit for breakfast only.

faqs.q: Can trekkers visit Hotel Everest View without staying?
faqs.a: Yes. Trekkers on the Namche rest day commonly walk up for tea, coffee or a meal on the terrace and continue to Khumjung. There is no entry fee, but prices for food and drinks are well above trail lodges.

faqs.q: Is Hotel Everest View the highest hotel in the world?
faqs.a: It was listed by Guinness World Records in 2004 as the highest-placed hotel, at about 3,880 m. Other lodges in the Himalaya and elsewhere are higher, but it remains one of the highest hotels with full hotel service and the most famous Everest view.

name: Yeti Mountain Home Lukla
summary: Yeti Mountain Home Lukla is a comfortable mountain lodge a few minutes from Tenzing-Hillary Airport, part of a small chain of upmarket lodges on the Everest trail. It offers ensuite rooms, electric blankets and a warm dining room, ideal before or after Lukla flights.
body: Yeti Mountain Home runs a chain of lodges in the Khumbu at Lukla, Phakding, Monjo, Namche, Thame and Kongde, spaced a short day's walk apart so that trekkers can sleep in comfort all the way to Namche and beyond. The Lukla lodge is built in stone and timber in a Sherpa style, close enough to the airport for the 6 am check-in that early flights demand. Rooms have attached bathrooms with hot water, good bedding and electric blankets, a real luxury after nights in teahouses.

On the way out, guests typically stay here the night before their flight back to Kathmandu or Ramechhap, settle tips with their crew and enjoy a proper hot shower. On the way in, it serves trekkers whose flights land late or who choose to start slowly. Meals in the dining room use local ingredients and vegetables from the lodge's greenhouse where available. In peak weeks Lukla fills with delayed trekkers, so booking ahead is essential.
why: Short walk to Lukla airport for early-morning flights
Ensuite rooms with hot water and electric blankets
Part of a lodge chain that lets you trek in comfort to Namche

faqs.q: Where are the Yeti Mountain Home lodges?
faqs.a: The chain has lodges at Lukla, Phakding, Monjo, Namche Bazaar, Thame and Kongde in the Everest region. They are spaced a short day's walk apart up to Namche, so a luxury trek can sleep in Yeti Mountain Homes for most nights below 3,500 m.

faqs.q: Do Yeti Mountain Home rooms have attached bathrooms?
faqs.a: Yes. Rooms at the Lukla lodge have attached bathrooms with hot water, plus electric blankets on the beds. This is a big step up from standard teahouses, where toilets are often shared and showers cost extra.

faqs.q: Is Yeti Mountain Home Lukla close to the airport?
faqs.a: Yes, it is a few minutes' walk from Tenzing-Hillary Airport, which matters for flight check-in around 6 am. If your flight is delayed by weather, it is a comfortable place to wait.

name: Yeti Mountain Home Namche
summary: Yeti Mountain Home Namche is an upmarket lodge on the eastern side of Namche Bazaar at about 3,440 m, with ensuite rooms, electric blankets and views towards Thamserku. It is a comfortable base for the two nights every Everest trek spends in Namche.
body: Namche is where most Everest treks spend two nights to acclimatise, so a good room here makes a real difference. Yeti Mountain Home's Namche lodge sits on the eastern side of the horseshoe-shaped town, a little away from the busiest lanes, with views across the Dudh Koshi gorge to Thamserku (6,623 m) and Kongde Ri. Rooms have attached bathrooms with hot showers, electric blankets and solid insulation, and the dining room has a sealed stove for warmth.

From the lodge, the acclimatisation hike to Syangboche, Hotel Everest View and Khumjung starts up the hill behind town, and the Sherpa Culture Museum, bakeries and shops are a short walk away. The lodge is used on our Everest luxury lodge trek and can be added to other itineraries on request. Beyond Namche the chain continues west to Thame and Kongde, but on the main Everest Base Camp trail, standard teahouses take over above here.
why: Ensuite rooms and electric blankets for two acclimatisation nights
Quieter eastern side of Namche with views to Thamserku
Easy access to the Hotel Everest View and Khumjung hike

faqs.q: Is Yeti Mountain Home Namche worth the extra cost?
faqs.a: For many travellers, yes. You spend two nights in Namche acclimatising, and a warm room with an attached bathroom, hot water and electric blankets helps you rest well. It suits couples, older trekkers and anyone wanting more comfort.

faqs.q: Can I book Yeti Mountain Home on a standard EBC trek?
faqs.a: Yes, we can upgrade the Lukla, Phakding and Namche nights to Yeti Mountain Home on request, subject to availability. Above Namche on the EBC route, accommodation returns to standard teahouses, with Everest Summit Lodge at Pangboche as a comfortable option.

faqs.q: How far is Yeti Mountain Home Namche from the centre?
faqs.a: It is on the eastern side of town, a few minutes' walk from the main lanes, shops and bakeries. The walk up to the museum and Syangboche starts nearby. Expect stone steps everywhere in Namche.

name: Panorama Lodge Namche
summary: Panorama Lodge is a family-run lodge on the upper terraces of Namche Bazaar, near the path to the Sherpa museum and Syangboche. It has ensuite rooms with mountain views, electric bed warmers and its own restaurant, at a mid-range price.
body: Panorama Lodge and Restaurant sits high on the Namche bowl, above most of the town's lanes and close to the trail that climbs to the national park visitor centre, Sherpa Culture Museum and Syangboche. The height gives it a wider outlook than lodges lower down, across the gorge to Thamserku and Kongde Ri, and a quieter feel at night. Climbing teams and trekking groups use it during the spring and autumn seasons.

Rooms have private bathrooms with hot water, electric bed warmers and seating areas, and the dining room serves Nepali and Western dishes, with a fireplace in the lounge. The trade-off for the views is a few extra minutes of stone steps from the main street, which is also useful acclimatisation. It is a good-value step up from basic teahouses for travellers who want an attached bathroom without the price of a luxury lodge.
why: Ensuite rooms with views across to Thamserku and Kongde
Upper terrace location close to the museum and Syangboche trail
Mid-range price with its own restaurant and warm lounge

faqs.q: Does Panorama Lodge Namche have attached bathrooms?
faqs.a: Yes, rooms have private bathrooms with hot water, plus electric bed warmers. This makes it a comfortable mid-range option for the two acclimatisation nights in Namche, at a lower price than luxury lodges.

faqs.q: Where is Panorama Lodge in Namche Bazaar?
faqs.a: On the upper terraces of Namche, near the path that climbs to the Sherpa Culture Museum, the national park visitor centre and Syangboche. Expect a few extra minutes of stone steps from the main street.

faqs.q: Is Panorama Lodge good for groups?
faqs.a: Yes. It is used by trekking and climbing groups in the main seasons and has a dining room and lounge large enough for groups. Book well ahead for October, November, April and May.

name: Everest Summit Lodge Pangboche
image_query: Everest Summit Lodge Pangboche Ama Dablam
summary: Everest Summit Lodge Pangboche is one of five upmarket lodges run by Everest Summit Lodges in the Khumbu. At about 4,000 m on the hillside above Pangboche, it has ensuite rooms, heated beds and a garden facing Ama Dablam and Everest.
body: Everest Summit Lodges operates five lodges in the region, at Lukla, Monjo, Mende, Tashinga and Pangboche. The Pangboche lodge is the highest on the main Everest Base Camp route, set on the hillside above the village with a direct view of Ama Dablam across the Imja valley and, on clear days, the summit of Everest above the Nuptse–Lhotse ridge. Rooms are ensuite with heated beds, and the lodge has a large dining room, a library corner and a garden of local plants.

On our luxury lodge trek we spend two nights here, using the middle day for a hike towards Ama Dablam base camp or to Upper Pangboche's old monastery. Standard EBC trekkers can also upgrade their Pangboche night here instead of sleeping at Dingboche, splitting the climb from Tengboche. Above Pangboche, accommodation is in standard teahouses only, so this is the last chance for real comfort on the way to base camp.
why: Highest upmarket lodge on the main Everest Base Camp trail
Ensuite rooms with heated beds and Ama Dablam views
Good base for the Ama Dablam base camp acclimatisation hike

faqs.q: Where are the Everest Summit Lodges?
faqs.a: Everest Summit Lodges runs five lodges in the Everest region: Lukla, Monjo, Mende above the Thame valley, Tashinga between Namche and Tengboche, and Pangboche. They are used on luxury lodge treks and can be booked on request.

faqs.q: How high is Everest Summit Lodge Pangboche?
faqs.a: It sits at about 4,000 m on the hillside above Pangboche village. Sleeping here after Namche and Tengboche or Tashinga gives a gradual climb. Altitude symptoms are still possible, so walk slowly and drink plenty of water.

faqs.q: Can I stay at Everest Summit Lodge Pangboche on the EBC trek?
faqs.a: Yes. We can book it instead of a Dingboche night, which adds a day to the trek but splits the climb more gently. Above Pangboche, all lodges on the route to base camp are standard teahouses.
